_meta.purpose: Canonical Cloudflare Workers deploy (REST API) metadata schema + binding shapes. Prevents repeated multipart-upload / binding-shape guessing failures.

worker_code_part.field_name: MUST exactly match metadata.main_module value (e.g. 'worker.js' or 'index.js' -- some Workers use index.js as main_module, not worker.js). Using the wrong field name causes 'Uncaught ReferenceError: __name is not defined' or SyntaxError at runtime because the code gets loaded under the wrong module name.

body_schema.main_module: string -- filename of the worker code part, e.g. worker.js

bindings.name: BINDING_NAME
bindings.text: REQUIRED when re-uploading -- omitting or leaving blank causes 'invalid or missing text property for bind'. If preserving an existing secret without knowing its value, do NOT include this binding in the metadata at all for THIS specific PUT unless the API confirms partial-binding PUTs preserve untouched secret_text bindings -- otherwise the secret is DELETED on redeploy. Prefer wrangler secret put for secret management instead of raw multipart re-upload.

known_gotchas:
Re-uploading a worker's existing code via GET (workers_get_worker_code) then PUT-ing it back can corrupt the code if the multipart response parser splits on a naive '

' search instead of the actual '

' MIME boundary separator -- this silently truncates the first few lines (commonly esbuild's __defProp/__name helper functions), producing 'Uncaught ReferenceError: __name is not defined' at runtime. FIX: parse using the exact CRLF-CRLF boundary, or better, use `wrangler deploy`/`versions upload` instead of manual multipart reconstruction whenever the original source is available.

Workers routes (custom domain routing) use the ZONE-level API endpoint, NOT account-level: GET/POST https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/{ZONE_ID}/workers/routes -- NOT /accounts/{id}/workers/routes.
wrangler r2 object put/get ALWAYS needs --remote. Omitting it silently targets a local Miniflare simulation and no-ops against the real bucket (looks like success, writes/reads nothing durable).

verification.rule: After any deploy claim, run npx wrangler deployments list --name <worker> to show the new deployment AND curl -sI the production route/workers.dev URL for the expected HTTP status. A 200 in the deploy API response body alone is NOT verification.
